answer: Each identity keeps a harbor safe by hunting fake ships — it earns a walnut of standing only when it correctly reports a Sybil identity, verified by established peers, and it is slashed when it wrongly accuses a real one. An umber of trust grows only from accurate reports, so a farm of a thousand fakes cannot hunt itself into standing: their reports are worthless because they are not established, and falsely accusing real identities strips their standing away, while one honest identity earns its place by catching one real fake at a time.
